title: General method for emulsion polymerization to yield functional terpolymers
author: Macbeth, Lin, et al.

steps.title: Assemble reactor for IDA neutralization
steps.instruction: Set up the 300 mL reactor as shown in Fig. 2 without a nitrogen line, plug the three free necks with rubber septum stoppers, and heat an oil bath to 65 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 2 M NaOH solution
steps.instruction: In a 250 mL beaker with a magnetic stir bar, dissolve 4 g NaOH pellets in 50 mL de‑ionized (DI) water, cover with Parafilm®, stir at 350 rpm for ~10 min until fully dissolved (exothermic).

steps.title: Neutralize IDA
steps.instruction: Add 6.055 g iminodiacetic acid (IDA) to the 50 mL 2 M NaOH solution, cover with Parafilm®, stir at 350 rpm for ~10 min until completely dissolved to give a 0.91 M neutralized‑IDA solution.

steps.title: Transfer neutralized IDA to reactor
steps.instruction: Pour the 50 mL neutralized‑IDA solution into the assembled reactor and start overhead stirring at 450 rpm.

steps.title: Add GMA dropwise
steps.instruction: Using a 10 mL mechanical pipette, place 6.821 mL glycidyl methacrylate (GMA) in the addition funnel, open the stopcock slightly and add to the reactor at ~1 drop / s, angling the funnel tip toward the centre of the flask; the mixture turns from colourless to white.

steps.title: Post‑addition reaction
steps.instruction: After the full GMA addition (final 0.91 M, 1:1 molar ratio GMA:IDA), replace the addition funnel with a rubber septum stopper and allow the reaction to proceed for 1 h.

steps.title: Neutralize crude product with HCl
steps.instruction: Using a 5 mL mechanical pipette, add 2 mL concentrated HCl to the reaction mixture, angling the pipette tip toward the centre to avoid loss of acid.

steps.title: Purify product by acetone washes
steps.instruction: Wash the crude product with acetone and water as follows:

substeps.instruction: i. Transfer the crude product and 300 mL acetone to a 500 mL separatory funnel; gently shake, vent pressure after each inversion until no pressure sound is heard.
ii. Let the funnel sit 5–10 min for phase separation; open the stopcock slightly and drain the bottom aqueous layer (contains product) while discarding the top organic layer.
iii. Repeat step ii with 50 mL DI water, keeping the aqueous layer and discarding the organic layer.
iv. Repeat steps i–iii three additional times, then perform a final wash with 300 mL acetone.
v. Dry the aqueous product in a vacuum desiccator for 20 min at room temperature to remove residual acetone.

steps.title: Store GMA‑IDA product
steps.instruction: Collect the clear, slightly viscous liquid and store at 4 °C (use amber vial or desiccant if light/moisture sensitive).

steps.title: Assemble reactor for BPM synthesis
steps.instruction: Set up the reactor with an addition funnel, nitrogen line, and ice bath; plug all free necks with rubber septum stoppers and position the agitator anchor as close to the bottom of the flask as possible.

steps.title: Purge reactor with nitrogen
steps.instruction: Purge the reactor and addition funnel with nitrogen, then close the nitrogen flow (continuous flow not required).

steps.title: Collect methacryloyl chloride air‑free
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 mL syringe cut at the 4 mL mark, wrap the cut end with Parafilm®, seal a rubber balloon over it with a cable tie, fill the balloon with nitrogen, attach a sparging needle, and collect 5 mL methacryloyl chloride using a 5 mL syringe (invert to remove bubbles). Wear appropriate gloves, goggles and respirator; work in a fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 % w/w NaOH solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the appropriate amount of NaOH pellets in DI water to make a 0.1 % (w/w) NaOH solution (as described in step 2 of the first preparation).

steps.title: Add diethyl ether and stir
steps.instruction: Add 150 mL diethyl ether to the reaction vessel, set overhead stirring to 450 rpm (note: test ether for peroxides every 6 months).

steps.title: Add 4‑hydroxybenzophenone
steps.instruction: Add 10.32 g 4‑hydroxybenzophenone to the vessel and homogenize for 10 min.

steps.title: Add triethylamine and purge
steps.instruction: Pipette 7.985 mL triethylamine into the vessel, then purge with nitrogen to achieve a 1:1 molar ratio of triethylamine to 4‑hydroxybenzophenone.

steps.title: Protect from light
steps.instruction: Cover the reaction vessel with foil, creating a peel‑back flap for monitoring, to keep the mixture in a light‑free environment.

steps.title: Load addition funnel with ether
steps.instruction: Add 25 mL diethyl ether to the addition funnel.

steps.title: Add methacryloyl chloride to funnel
steps.instruction: Introduce the previously collected 5 mL methacryloyl chloride into the ether‑filled addition funnel (sparging needle already in ether to aid homogenization).

steps.title: Add reagents dropwise
steps.instruction: Open the addition‑funnel stopcock and add the ether‑methacryloyl chloride mixture dropwise to the reaction until a 1:1:1 molar ratio of methacryloyl chloride:triethylamine:4‑hydroxybenzophenone is reached; the solution becomes a white liquid. Replace the funnel with a rubber septum and let the reaction proceed in the dark for 18 h.

steps.title: Filter triethylammonium chloride precipitate
steps.instruction: After 18 h, filter the mixture through filter paper in a glass funnel to remove the solid triethylammonium hydrochloride (product should be a white liquid, not a yellow solid).

steps.title: Wash filtrate with water and NaOH
steps.instruction: Wash the filtrate sequentially with 200 mL DI water then 200 mL 0.1 % NaOH, repeating the extraction (as in Part I) until the organic phase shows no yellow colour.

steps.title: Dry over magnesium sulfate
steps.instruction: Add excess anhydrous MgSO₄ to the organic layer with a metal scooper, swirl, and repeat additions until a “snowstorm” effect is observed (MgSO₄ freely flowing).

steps.title: Evaporate diethyl ether
steps.instruction: Remove diethyl ether under reduced pressure using a Buchner funnel; the residue should be a white solid (BPM).

steps.title: Dry and store BPM
steps.instruction: Dry the BPM solid in a vacuum desiccator for 3 days, then store in a sealed, foil‑covered vessel in refrigeration.

steps.title: Assemble reactor for copolymerization
steps.instruction: Set up the reactor with a nitrogen line and oil bath, heat the bath to 70 °C, and plug the free necks with rubber septum stoppers.

steps.title: Add GMA‑IDA and initiator
steps.instruction: Add 2.7 g GMA‑IDA and 0.39 g potassium persulfate (KPS) to the reactor together with 126 mL DI water; stir at 450 rpm to obtain a 10:1 molar ratio of monomer to initiator.

steps.title: Add BPM solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.4 g BPM in 10.8 mL butyl acrylate (BA) and charge the solution into the reactor to achieve a total monomer ratio of 7:1:1 (BA:GMA‑IDA:BPM).

steps.title: Polymerization under nitrogen
steps.instruction: Start nitrogen flow, raise the oil bath to 70 °C, cover the reactor with foil, and allow the emulsion polymerization to proceed in the dark for 20 h.

steps.title: Centrifuge crude polymer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the crude product at 3000 g for 15 min; repeat the centrifugation twice more, discarding the polymer sediment each time.

steps.title: Dialysis to remove GMA‑IDA
steps.instruction: Perform dialysis for 3 h using 20 kDa tubing:

substeps.instruction: i. Cut tubing to required length, leaving 5–6 cm extra for clips.
ii. Soak tubing in DI water for 10 min.
iii. Fold one end, clip, load the polymer solution, and clip the other end.
iv. Place tubing in 1 L DI water (magnetic stir bar, 350 rpm).

steps.title: Dialysis to remove BA and BPM
steps.instruction: Repeat the dialysis procedure (steps i–v) substituting DI water with methanol to remove residual BA and BPM.

steps.title: Final centrifugation and storage
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the purified retentate twice more at 3000 g for 15 min, collect the supernatant, and store the final copolymer in a refrigerator.

To verify that the copolymer is curable via exposure to UV irradiation, monitor the absorption spectrum at 270–290 nm as the coating is being exposed to UV-light (365 nm). The absorption band at 270 nm should decrease as a result of successful benzophenone crosslinking as shown in Fig. 8. To verify the copolymer contained poly(n‑butyl acrylate) and GMA functionalized with IDA ligands, take ATR-FTIR and absorbance spectra of polypropylene coated with the copolymer compared to bare polypropylene as the control as shown in Fig. 9. Bare polypropylene should show absorption bands at 3000–2800 cm-1 for the C—H stretch and at 1450 cm-1 and 1370 cm-1 for the C—H bend. For the copolymer film, absorption band at 3000–2800 cm-1 for the C—H stretch and a strong absorption band at 1710 cm-1 for the carbonyl stretch and bands at 1260–1160 cm-1 for a ether stretch indicate poly(n‑butyl acrylate) is present while a small shoulder at shoulder at 1620 cm-1 indicate the presence of IDA ligands [3].
